_readme: SHARED CORPUS. Two implementations of 'paragraph 1 of the body' must agree:
BOTH read this file. A change to EITHER implementation must be reflected here,
and a case may only be added once both sides produce the expected lede.
Two independently hand-written test corpora is exactly how the pair drifted:
Python's str.strip()/\s and JavaScript's trim()/\s classify different characters
(Python does not treat U+FEFF as whitespace, JavaScript does not treat U+001C as
whitespace), so the card rendered as prose a heading the backend had budgeted as
a heading. Both sides therefore trim SPACES AND TABS ONLY and treat a blank line
as spaces and tabs only, which is CommonMark's own rule and depends on neither
Write every control and Unicode character as an explicit \uXXXX escape. A literal
invisible character in this file cannot be reviewed.

PENDING as of this commit: only the backend half reads this file. unit-card.tsx::ledeOf still splits on /
\s*
/ and trims with trim(), so it disagrees with three cases below - the two U+FEFF cases and the U+00A0 one. It needs /
[ 	]*
/ and a trim of spaces and tabs only.
